scope: Parent evidence about the running Engram process and about what a graceful stop does to WAL sidecars. The checkpoint test ran on a private cp -a copy of ~/.engram, never on the real directory.

running_process.supervision: not a systemd unit; lives in transient scope app-Hyprland-xdg\x2dterminal\x2dexec-6edb38c6.scope created by xdg-terminal-exec, so it was launched from a terminal session
running_process.implication: The HTTP API on port 7437 serves the shared store to whatever other tooling uses it; nothing about this process is specific to isSWF.

before.compatibility: exit 2, unsafe or invalid fixture metadata

conclusions: The store is healthy: integrity_check ok and 28 tables on a faithful copy.
The 27 MB WAL folds into engram.db when the last connection closes cleanly, and SQLite then removes -wal and -shm.
The preflight rejection is a side effect of the store being open, not a defect in the data.
Stopping Engram gracefully should therefore make `compatibility` succeed against the real path; the rejection returns as soon as any process reopens the store.
push_versus_sidecars: These are unrelated mechanisms and the earlier report mixed them. -wal/-shm exist because a process has the store open in WAL mode. The push is the separate autosync feature configured on that process.
real_store_effect: None. Only a read-only copy was opened; ~/.engram kept identical sizes and mtimes for db, sidecars, identity and locks.
limits: The copy was taken while the store was open, so it is not an atomic snapshot and says nothing about writes that had not reached the WAL. A passing preflight after stop is a point-in-time observation, not a guarantee about concurrent writers. No memory contents were inspected.
